_readme: Concept bank for the Hamdam Instagram reel series. The agent READS this file and never writes to it. After a concept ships, set used=true by hand - and verify against live captions, because the flag has drifted before.
_verification_status: DRAFT - Persian lesson and send lines drafted by Claude, reviewed by Ealia. Arguments and insights carry _check notes. Nothing here has published yet.
_selection_rule: Weighted to Rumi and Khayyam - the two poets with international recognition - and chosen for ORDINARY DAILY CONCERN rather than metaphysics. Poets alternate so rotation never blocks. All screened clear of wine imagery per hard rule 5. NOTE the evidence: on YouTube, Saadi's Bani Adam took 1,126 views and Rumi's obscure Nur-e Khorshid took 16 - recognition of the SPECIFIC VERSE matters more than fame of the poet.
_page_note: Reel pages: 1 headline, 2 lesson + send/reflect prompt, 3 the philological point, 4 Persian verse, 5 English translation with poet line. Stage 0 is not rendered. Recognition hooks; the argument rewards whoever stays. insightEn, lessonEn, sendEn and headline are Latin script ONLY - Source Serif has no Arabic glyphs.
_prompt_principles: Send prompts name the RELATIONSHIP, never the recipient's flaw. The sender must come out generous, not superior. Test it by reading it as the RECIPIENT: chosen, or diagnosed? Verses that assert how things are get promptType 'reflect' - a question that earns a comment - instead of a send prompt.
_sendability_test: BEFORE writing a send prompt, ask WHO THE POEM POINTS AT. This decides sendability, not the theme. (a) Points at the READER'S OWN FAILING - self-accusation. Never sendable: forwarding it says 'this is about your flaw'. Use promptType 'reflect' with a question. (b) Points at SOMETHING SHARED - sendable; the sender is saying 'this is us'. (c) Points WARMLY AT THE RECIPIENT - sendable; the sender is saying 'this is you'. A warm prompt bolted onto a self-accusing poem reads as false and is worse than no prompt. Worked example: rumi-022 is Rumi catching HIMSELF being cruel - 'we taunted him'. Pairing it with 'for someone who is kind to everyone' failed this test and was corrected on 1 Sep 2026.
_cta_principle_addendum: A send prompt that DESCRIBES the recipient ('for someone who does not grieve the past') is an appraisal, and appraisals do not get forwarded - the sender has to decide the label is true, and the recipient reads it as a claim about themselves. The strongest form is FIRST PERSON PLURAL: the sender acts on the poem and includes the recipient in it. 'Let us not grieve yesterday and tomorrow' works where 'for someone who does not grieve them' does not. Use the poem's own words wherever possible.
_seasonal_note: Check the hemisphere before scheduling any verse with seasonal imagery. The audience is largely Australian diaspora; posting about winter ending in September reads as copied from a northern account.
_context_rule: Only use verses whose meaning is complete in the lines shown. A two-line fragment whose sense depends on the surrounding ghazal cannot carry an argument - rumi-028 was drafted and dropped on 1 Sep 2026 because the insight claimed something ('many have sat here before you') that the couplet does not actually say. Self-contained quatrains are safest.
_mood_key: happy = bright Mahur; love = romantic Mahur; grave = restrained, sparse; wry = light but not celebratory. Never put a bright bed under a grave concept.

concepts.headline: TWO DAYS I REFUSE TO WORRY ABOUT
concepts.argument:
Khayyam does not say seize the day. Read the last two lines: he names two specific days and refuses both of them.

The day that has not come. The day that has gone. Those are the only two he has ever declined to grieve over - which leaves exactly one day standing, and he never has to mention it.

That is a sharper piece of construction than the carpe diem line English usually gives him. He does not argue for the present. He simply subtracts the other two and lets you notice what is left.
concepts.insightFa: خیام نمی‌گوید «دم را دریاب» — دو روز را نام می‌برد و هر دو را کنار می‌گذارد
concepts.insightEn: Khayyam never says seize the day. He names two days and refuses both, and lets you notice what is left.
concepts.lessonFa: دو روز را نمی‌شود زندگی کرد: دیروز و فردا
concepts.lessonEn: Two days cannot be lived: yesterday and tomorrow
concepts.sendFa: بیا غم دیروز و فردا را نخوریم
concepts.sendEn: Let's not grieve yesterday and tomorrow
concepts._check: Self-contained quatrain - no surrounding ghazal needed. The claim is a plain reading of lines 3-4. No season, no wine, no divine addressee. Points at something SHARED. sendFa uses the couplet's own vocabulary and is FIRST PERSON PLURAL - Ealia's phrasing, flipped from second to first person 1 Sep 2026.

concepts.headline: THE PLAN WAS NOT MADE WITH YOU
concepts.argument:
Khayyam is not comforting you. Read the last line again: the arrangement was made without consulting you.

That is an odd thing to find consoling, and yet it is. If the plan was never yours to approve, then the worry you are carrying about it was never doing any work. He is not saying it will be fine. He is saying your anxiety has no job here.

English versions of Khayyam usually soften this into wistfulness. The Persian is drier and more practical than that.
concepts.insightFa: خیام دلداری نمی‌دهد؛ می‌گوید تصمیم بی تو گرفته شده — و همین آزادت می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: Khayyam is not offering comfort. He says the decision was made without you - and that is what frees you.
concepts.lessonFa: بعضی چیزها را بی‌مشورت تو چیده‌اند
concepts.lessonEn: Some things were arranged without asking you
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که با او می‌شود از نگرانی‌ها گفت
concepts.sendEn: For someone you can talk your worries through with
concepts._check: Interpretation of the closing line, not an assertion about Khayyam's philosophy. Safe as phrased.

concepts.headline: TOMORROW IS NOT YOURS YET
concepts.argument:
The word Khayyam uses is dastras - ordinary Persian for within reach, the word you would use about a shop or a phone. Not a philosophical term at all.

So the line is not a meditation on time. It is a practical observation: tomorrow is not available to you. You cannot get at it. Whatever you are doing with it in your head right now, you are handling something that is not in the room.

Translations reach for grander language and lose exactly that plainness.
concepts.insightFa: «دسترس» واژهٔ روزمره است، نه فلسفی — خیام می‌گوید فردا در دسترس تو نیست
concepts.insightEn: Dastras is everyday Persian for within reach. Not a philosophical claim - a practical one.
concepts.lessonFa: فردا هنوز به دست تو نیست
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که امروز کنارت است
concepts.sendEn: For someone who is beside you today
concepts._check: dastras as everyday register is the claim to check - worth one native reader's eye on whether it read the same way in the 11th century.

concepts.headline: WHAT AUTUMN TOOK, SPRING REPAYS
concepts.argument:
Two lines, and the whole consolation sits in one verb.

Rumi does not say spring is generous, or that it makes up for autumn. He says it repays - the Persian is a debt word, the one you use for settling an account. Autumn took something that was never its own to keep. Spring is not doing you a kindness; it is returning what was owed.

That is a colder and better thought than the greeting-card version.
concepts.insightFa: ادا کردن واژهٔ بدهی است — بهار بخشش نمی‌کند، حساب صاف می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: The verb is a debt word. Spring is not being generous - it is settling an account.
concepts.lessonFa: آنچه پاییز برد، بهار پس می‌دهد
concepts.lessonEn: What autumn took, spring gives back
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که زمستان سختی را پشت سر گذاشته
concepts.sendEn: For someone who has come through a hard winter
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: HOLD - SEASONAL. It is September in Sydney (spring), so a line about winter ending reads as borrowed from a northern account. Schedule when the seasons match. ada kardan as a debt verb is the claim worth a native reader's eye.

concepts.headline: WHY HAVE YOU FROZEN IN THAT CORNER
concepts.argument:
One verb carries this line, and it repeats: to turn.

Rumi asks why you have stopped turning - and then names the thing that has you stuck, which is not sadness itself but a thought that only ever revolves around sadness. The distinction matters. He is not telling you to be happy. He is pointing out that you are still moving, just in a circle of one subject.
concepts.insightFa: مولانا نمی‌گوید غم نخور؛ می‌گوید تو داری می‌گردی، اما فقط دور یک چیز
concepts.insightEn: Rumi does not say stop grieving. He says you are still turning - just around one subject.
concepts.lessonEn: Turning is easier than standing still
concepts.sendFa: چه چیزی دوباره به حرکتت می‌آورد؟
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: RECLASSIFIED to reflect 1 Sep 2026 - the poem points at the reader's own stuckness, so sending it reads as 'I have noticed you are depressed'. Fails the sendability test.

concepts.headline: STILL NO MASTER
concepts.argument:
A quatrain is built to arrive somewhere. Three lines set it up and the fourth lands.

This one refuses. Khayyam spends three lines describing a life of study and constraint, and then the fourth line admits he has not learned the trade. The form promises wisdom and the content declines to supply any.

Which is the point. It is a poem about the gap between how long you have been at something and how much you actually know - and it is eleventh century.
concepts.insightFa: رباعی قرار است در مصراع چهارم به حکمت برسد — این یکی اعتراف می‌کند که نرسیده
concepts.insightEn: A quatrain is built to arrive at wisdom in its fourth line. This one admits it has not.
concepts.lessonFa: سال‌ها شاگردی کردم و هنوز استاد نیستم
concepts.lessonEn: Years a student, and still no master
concepts.sendFa: تو در چه کاری هنوز شاگردی؟
concepts.sendEn: What are you still a student of?
concepts._check: That the rubai turn lands in the fourth line is standard description of the form. Reflect, not send - 'I am not good enough' is not something you forward to a friend.

concepts.headline: LOOK DOWN ON NO ONE
concepts.argument:
Notice the order. Rumi does not begin with the advice - he begins by admitting that he was one of the people doing the taunting.

We did not think this of him, and yet we mocked him. Only then: look upon no human being with contempt.

Advice that arrives after a confession lands differently from advice that arrives from above. He is not instructing you from a height. He is telling you what he got wrong.
concepts.insightFa: مولانا اول اعتراف می‌کند که خودش طعنه می‌زده — نصیحت بعد از اعتراف می‌آید
concepts.insightEn: Rumi admits he did the taunting himself. The advice comes after the confession, not from above it.
concepts.sendFa: آخرین بار کی دربارهٔ کسی زود قضاوت کردی؟
concepts.sendEn: When did you last judge someone too quickly?
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: RECLASSIFIED to reflect 1 Sep 2026 - self-accusation, so it is not sendable. The confession-then-advice order is visible in the text. Closest verse in the queue to Saadi's Bani Adam in register.
